issues.description: The template declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) but the problem statement (and UML) specify addGuestStudents(int): void. The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch between the template and the specification/solution can confuse students about the correct method signature and may cause them to implement the wrong method or add an overload unintentionally.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the specification: change public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If validation behavior is desired, either implement validation inside that single-parameter method or provide a private helper; ensure the public API matches the problem statement and UML. Alternatively, if the extra boolean parameter was intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int, boolean).

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define an addGuestStudents(int) method, but the template provides addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The extra boolean parameter in the template changes the method signature students are expected to implement and will create confusion about the required API and how to call/implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing it to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement the method body accordingly (or, if validation is desired, implement validation internally without altering the public signature).
